Standard: The air vehicle refueling systems and components meet operational, proof, and ultimate pressure requirements. a. Boom Tanker. At least 120 (-5) psi operational, 240 (-10) psi proof, 360 psi ultimate (burst). b. Drogue Tanker. At least 120 (-5) psi operational, 240 (-10) psi proof, 360 psi ultimate (burst). c. Receptacle Receiver. At least 90 (-3) psi operational, 180 (-6) psi proof, 270 psi ultimate (burst). d. Probe Receiver. At least 60 (-3) psi operational, 120 (-6) psi proof, 180 psi ultimate (burst). Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examination of component and system specifications shows AR subsystem is designed to meet operational, proof, and ultimate pressures. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis of AR system design and component qualification reports verifies system is qualified to the proof and ultimate pressures. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Lab testing of components and fuel subsystem/test rig verifies AR components and subsystems can withstand pressure limits. The components, individually, and the system are capped and pressurized up to the positive proof pressure limit for five minutes and then depressurized. The system is inspected for any signs of structural deformation and leakage. The system is also proof pressure tested to its negative limit in the same fashion. If the system cannot be pressure tested as a whole, then it is acceptable to test the system in multiple parts ensuring the breaks in the system are not areas of concern.
    (2) Ground test: Air vehicle ground testing of AR subsystems verifies AR components and subsystems can withstand pressure limits. The system is capped and pressurized up to the positive proof pressure limit for five minutes and then depressurized. The system is inspected for any signs of structural deformation and leakage. The system is performance tested. The system is also proof pressure tested to its negative limit in the same fashion. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (3) Flight test: Flight testing with targeted air vehicle verifies maximum pressures does not exceed fuel system proof pressures and shows no unexpected fuel leakage, no permanent deformation or failures of fuel systems or components of either air vehicle involved in the refueling process.
